Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. Shubman Gill and his men have made their way out to the centre. It will be the left-hand, right-hand opening combination of Sediqullah Atal and Abdul Malik for Afghanistan. Mohammed Siraj will kickstart proceedings with the new ball. Malik is on strike. Three slips and a gully await. Here we go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

A mountain to climb - Afghanistan will have to put the disappointment of that long bowling effort behind them as they begin the daunting task of tracking down India's first-innings total of 564. The visitors will need to draw on all of their first-class experience and show plenty of patience against a well-rounded Indian attack. Given the movement Mohammad Saleem was able to extract even with the older ball, India's quicks will be eager to have a crack with the new one. Stay tuned for Afghanistan's reply.

What might have been - For Afghanistan, there was a lion-hearted effort from Mohammad Saleem, who kept charging in despite the energy-sapping conditions and was rewarded with a maiden five-wicket haul before eventually finishing with six wickets. Ziaur Rahman and Azmatullah Omarzai bowled well in patches too, but Afghanistan were ultimately left to rue their decision-making with the DRS. Afghanistan's cause was not helped by the injury to left-arm spin bowling all-rounder Sharafuddin Ashraf, who left the field on Day 1 and did not return. Whether he is fit enough to take any further part in the match remains to be seen

Contributions across the board - Having opted to bat first, KL Rahul and Shubman Gill were the two centurions in the Indian innings. Sai Sudharsan and Rishabh Pant both fell in the 80s, while Dhruv Jurel also looked in fine touch during his stay at the crease. Manav Suthar and Mohammed Siraj also chipped in with useful runs, while Washington Sundar played an impressive hand to take India past 550.

India have declared - Shubman Gill calls his men back as he feels that they have got enough runs on the board. It was a long and gruelling stint in the field for Afghanistan in scorching conditions, but there was no shortage of effort from the tourists throughout the innings. Mohammad Saleem leads his side off the park with the ball held aloft after a wholehearted effort.

How much more will India add? With two left-handers at the crease, expect Nangeyalia Kharote to play a much bigger role in the second session as the tourists look to bowl India out. The left-arm spinner will have his eyes on the rough that has started to develop around the left-handers' off stump. We will be back at 12.10 pm IST (6.40 am GMT) for the start of the second session. See you then!

Saleem made the difference - Shubman Gill would have been out lbw, while Rishabh Pant had also nicked one behind, but Afghanistan opted against reviewing on both occasions. It was Mohammad Saleem who led the way with the lengths he bowled with the new ball. While Omarzai did create those two chances, he still erred a touch on the shorter side at times. Saleem managed to strike twice before Hashmatullah Shahidi managed to prise out Pant.

A session of mixed fortunes - Just three wickets fell on the entirety of Day 1, but Afghanistan matched that tally in the morning session alone. Even so, India added 107 runs in 25 overs to push their total close to 500. After letting their quicks loosen up, Afghanistan took the second new ball. Azmatullah Omarzai created a couple of opportunities, but for the second day running, the visitors were left to rue their use of the DRS.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to get going. Another testing day awaits the players under what are expected to be demanding conditions. Hashmatullah Shahidi has his men in a huddle near the ropes for one final word before they take the field. They are followed by Shubman Gill and Rishabh Pant. Afghanistan are starting with the old ball. Ziaur Rahman will open the attack. Gill is on strike. Here we go...

A quick word with India's number 3 - Sai Sudharsan says he was well set and feels it could have been a much bigger innings. While disappointed not to convert it into a hundred, he is happy to have made a meaningful contribution to the team's cause. On the switch from white-ball to red-ball cricket, Sudharsan says there is not a huge mental difference. He believes it comes down to decision-making and making a few minor adjustments to suit the format. Sai shares that he spent time watching videos and preparing for what the Afghan bowlers might try. More than anything, it was about trusting himself and backing his game, something he feels helped him throughout the innings.

PITCH REPORT - Former India wicketkeeper, Deep Dasgupta is alongside former Australia captain Michael Clarke. Clarke notes that the middle of the pitch still looks almost brand new, with only a couple of ball marks visible. He points out that it is a touch drier closer to the crease and expects the rough to become a little more pronounced by the end of the day. Michael feels the surface played slightly slow and low on Day 1 and expects more of the same today. His advice to the bowlers is simple - attack the stumps. Dasgupta agrees with Clarke's assessment. He believes it remains a very good wicket for batting, though it could get slower with time.

Afghanistan's search for wickets - For Hashmatullah Shahidi and his side, a fresh day brings renewed hope after a gruelling 85 overs in the field. The visitors know that early wickets are the only currency that can buy them a way back into this contest. If their bowling attack fails to strike in the first hour, they risk chasing shadows for the rest of the day. Afghanistan’s primary objective for the morning is to win the first session by executing disciplined lines, exploiting any early moisture, and breaking the ominous Gill-Pant partnership. The scoring rate in the first session will provide a fair idea about India's thought process. An exciting day of Test cricket awaits.

Will Pant cut loose? Resuming the action alongside Gill is Rishabh Pant, who has played a fascinatingly uncharacteristic innings so far. Known for his explosive and high-risk boundary-hitting, Pant curbed his natural instincts on Day 1 to grind out an unbeaten 50. His disciplined approach added immense stability to the Indian middle order during the final session. All eyes will be on the wicketkeeper-batter this morning to see if he continues this patient job or unleashes his trademark aggressive style.

Greetings, all! Welcome to Day 2 of this one-off Test. India finished the opening day in a position of absolute authority, racking up a commanding 368 for 3 after 85 overs. The home side's batting depth was on full display as two batters notched up magnificent centuries. KL Rahul anchored the innings beautifully with a 100 before his dismissal, while Shubman Gill remained unblemished, finishing the day unbeaten on 103. They were well-supported by Sai Sudharsan, who missed out on a maiden Test ton with a brilliant 81.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Afghanistan search for a way back - With their pacers being tired, the visitors opted against taking the second new ball late in the day, but expect them to take it straight away on the second morning. It is imperative that they make the new ball count if they are to prevent India from batting them out of the contest. Rishabh Pant was uncharacteristically restrained during his stay at the crease, and whether the handbrake comes off on Day 2 remains to be seen. Ideally, the hosts will want to bat once, bat big and put Afghanistan under immense scoreboard pressure. Join us again on Sunday, June 7, with the first ball on Day 2 set to be bowled at 9.30 am IST (4 am GMT). Until then, take care and goodbye!

Gill and Rahul led the charge - After India won the toss, KL Rahul had to tussle early in his innings against the slower nature of the surface, but he gradually grew in confidence and eventually brought up a well-crafted century. Sai Sudharsan looked positive from the outset and played fluently throughout his stay at the crease before falling short of what would have been his maiden Test hundred. Both batters rode their luck with Rahul nicking one behind when he was on 16, but Afghanistan opted against a review, while Rahmanullah Gurbaz put down a tough chance when Sudharsan was on 20. Shubman Gill looked in complete control during his stay at the crease, and with Afghanistan's bowlers beginning to tire in the final session, Gill and Rishabh Pant combined to press home India's advantage.

Afghanistan were made to work hard - The tourists showed promising signs with the new ball, but whatever little moisture was on offer in the morning gradually disappeared. That left the bowlers with very little assistance from the surface thereafter. That said, Afghanistan's quicks deserve plenty of credit. Despite the extreme heat, they kept plugging away throughout the day, with Ziaur Rahman and Mohammad Saleem looking the most likely to create opportunities. The debutant left-arm spinner, Nangeyalia Kharote, initially struggled with his consistency, but during the final hour or so, he began to find the right areas with greater regularity.

Let's hear from one of the centurions - KL Rahul says that he is feeling really happy to have spent some time in the middle and to have made the switch from T20 to Test in a really short time. Adds that the ball was not coming on nicely, and the track looked slow, which was expected by them after the training we had here. KL reckons that there is no better thing than spending time in the middle, as that's the best way you can assess a track or conditions. Rahul says that he has changed his style in the T20 format and believes that not having much turnaround time sometimes helps as well. Shares that in the morning session, he played a few more shots than he would normally, but he isn't angry because such things happen. Feels the track will assist good bowling, and the spinners will come into play as the cracks have started to open.

A dominant day for India - Headlined by centuries from Shubman Gill and KL Rahul, the home side cashed in on conditions that did not trouble the batters much beyond the opening session. It was a tough day at the office for Afghanistan, where they could not put it together with the ball for long periods. The inexperience of a side still finding its feet in Test cricket was evident at times, but these are the kind of days that can prove invaluable in the long run.

India primed for final session onslaught - The unbeaten duo of KL Rahul and Shubman Gill safely navigated the remaining overs before the Tea interval to keep India firmly in the driver’s seat. Rahul is currently anchoring the innings masterfully and closing in on a well-deserved century, while Gill looks comfortable at the other end. With the scorecard reflecting deep batting dominance and wickets well in hand, the Indian team is in a prime position to accelerate the scoring rate and maximise their advantage in the final session of the day. We will be back with the final session on Day 1 at 2.30 pm IST (9 am GMT).

Saleem broke the century partnership - Just when India looked ready to bat Afghanistan completely out of the session, the visitors managed a crucial breakthrough. Afghanistan bowler Mohammad Saleem provided the solitary moment of joy for his side by breaking the dangerous 139-run stand. He managed to find the edge of Sai's bat, resulting in a sharp catch from the wicketkeeper. Despite the setback, Sai's departure for a well-made 81 brought Shubman Gill to the crease, who quickly settled nerves alongside an unflappable Rahul.

Rahul and Sai dominate the post-Lunch session - India capitalized on their solid start, coming out after Lunch with aggressive intent to put Afghanistan on the back foot. Resuming at 96 for 1 after 25 overs, KL Rahul spearheaded the attack by punishing loose deliveries and turning the strike over effortlessly as India head into the break at 209 for 2 after 50 overs. Together with Sai, Rahul shifted the momentum into overdrive as the pair stitched together a rapid, high-scoring partnership. Both batters played with authority, seamlessly rotating the strike and finding the boundaries to cross their respective half-centuries in quick succession.

TEA ON DAY 1 - 25 overs were bowled in this session, where India scored 113 runs for the loss of 1 wicket. India continue to remain firmly in control of proceedings. There was certainly no shortage of effort from Afghanistan in the field, but they have struggled to sustain pressure for long enough.

Looking ahead - Afghanistan's spinners were able to find a bit of grip and turn from the surface, and perhaps they could have been a touch more aggressive with their field placements. By allowing India's batters easy singles down the ground, they relieved much of the pressure that had been built up. Whether Afghanistan make that change in the afternoon session remains to be seen. Given the oppressive heat, short and sharp spells from the seamers will likely be the order of the day. The second session will commence at 12.10 pm IST (6.40 am GMT). See you then!

Tale post the opening exchanges - Yashasvi Jaiswal was the first to fall, handing Mohammad Saleem his maiden Test wicket. Jaiswal's departure brought Sai Sudharsan to the crease. Unlike KL Rahul, who initially found timing the ball a challenge, Sudharsan looked more assured from the outset. The left-hander did enjoy a slice of fortune, though, when Rahmanullah Gurbaz put down a tough chance on 20.

The opening session goes India's way - The talk from Hashmatullah Shahidi after losing the toss was about starting well, and while the visitors may have only one wicket to show for their efforts, they did not bowl as badly as the scoreboard might suggest. There was not a great deal of assistance on offer from the surface, but to their credit, Afghanistan's new-ball attack started impressively. Ziaur Rahman, in particular, looked threatening. By going wide of the crease and creating that inward angle into the right-hander, he consistently had KL Rahul in two minds. In fact, he even created a genuine opportunity when Rahul nicked one behind while on 16, but Afghanistan opted against the review and the chance went begging.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the national anthems, and we are all set to get going. It is a sparse crowd at the moment, but expect more spectators to filter in as the day progresses. The bell has been rung to signify the imminent start of play. A few final words from the Afghanistan captain, Hashmatullah Shahidi, in the team huddle as he gathers his players before they take the field. It will be the left-hand, right-hand combination of Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul to open the innings for India. It will be the right-arm quick, Ziaur Rahman to deliver the first over of the game. Jaiswal will take strike. Two slips and a gully await. Let's go...
Before we get underway, the match officials and the two teams will line up for the national anthems. It will be Afghanistan's national anthem first, followed by that of India.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Sediqullah Atal, Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Abdul Malik, Rahmat Shah, Hashmatullah Shahidi (C), Afsar Zazai (WK), Azmatullah Omarzai, Sharafuddin Ashraf, Nangeyalia Kharote (On debut), Ziaur Rahman and Mohammad Saleem.

India (Playing XI) - KL Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Sai Sudharsan, Shubman Gill (C), Rishabh Pant (WK), Dhruv Jurel, Washington Sundar, Manav Suthar (On debut), Kuldeep Yadav, Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna.

The skipper of Afghanistan - Hashmatullah Shahidi says that they would have batted first as well. Adds that the toss is not in their hands, so the focus now is on playing good cricket and starting the match well. Shahidi acknowledges that his side does not get enough opportunities to play Test cricket, but insists they are ready for the challenge. He says the team is well prepared after a productive training camp back home and is looking forward to the contest. Hashmatullah says former coach Jonathan Trott played a huge role in Afghanistan's growth in Test cricket, but now it is time for Richard Pybus, and the team is excited about the new chapter. He describes the new coach as a positive influence and hopes the players can continue to learn and improve under his guidance. On team combination, Shahidi informs that Afghanistan have gone in with three seamers and two spinners, and there is a debut for Nangeyalia Kharote.

The captain of India - Shubman Gill opts to bat first, citing the hot, humid conditions, which will make the surface slow and low as the game goes on. Gill shares that it is a special feeling for him to captain India on home soil. Shubman reckons the preparations have been really good, they've had a good couple of days' rest, and the players are ready to go. Adds that they have got a few Test matches at home and they'll be looking to get the combinations right. Gill informs that Manav Suthar is making his debut.

TOSS - Shubman Gill has made his way out for the flip of the coin. He is joined by his Afghanistan counterpart, Hashmatullah Shahidi. 'Heads' is the call from Shahidi, but it has come down as a Tail. India opt to BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Former Australian captain, Michael Clarke is pitchside. He says this looks like a wonderful batting surface and is full of praise for both the ground and the pitch. Clarke notes that while there could be some deterioration as the Test progresses, the first couple of days should be excellent for batting. Michael observes a bit of dryness at one end and, looking at the middle of the surface, he expects a touch of moisture. Overall, though, he feels it is a very good batting wicket. In his view, it is the sort of surface where batters will need to put in the hard yards early, but once set, they can make the most of the conditions and cash in. Former Indian wicketkeeper, Deep Dasgupta largely echoes Michael Clarke's assessment of the surface. He feels the extra moisture and the grass left on the pitch are largely a response to the extreme weather, with temperatures expected to go beyond 40 degrees Celsius over the course of the Test. Deep agrees that there could be a bit of moisture, which should provide some encouragement for the fast bowlers.

Debut alert - Manav Suthar has been handed his maiden India cap by Kuldeep Yadav in the team huddle. A moment to cherish for the 23-year-old left-arm spin bowling all-rounder from Rajasthan, who gets his first opportunity in Test cricket. There is a debut in the Afghanistan camp as well, and it is another left-arm spin bowling all-rounder. Nangeyalia Kharote has received his Test cap from the Afghanistan bowling coach, Hamid Hassan.

Opportunity knocks for both sides - India and Afghanistan have met only once before in Test cricket, a one-sided affair in Bengaluru back in 2018. Seven years later, Afghanistan arrive with far more experience and belief than they did on that historic occasion. India are rebuilding, Afghanistan are hungry, and Mullanpur’s pitch is an unknown for now. Will India’s new-look lineup find stability and dominance at home? Or can Afghanistan, armed with nothing to lose and a point to prove, add another memorable chapter to their young Test journey? Toss and team news to follow...

Afghanistan’s red-ball story - For the visiting side, this is about exposure and evolution. Since gaining Test status in 2017, they have played just 12 matches, but already boast four wins. Captain Hashmatullah Shahidi leads a 15-member squad back in whites after a tough outing against Zimbabwe, and the absence of Rashid Khan and Ibrahim Zadran opens doors for others. Sediqullah Atal and Azmatullah Omarzai are back to strengthen the middle order, while uncapped all-rounder Nangeyalia Kharote could get a Test cap. With limited red-ball cricket under their belt, Afghanistan’s goal is simple - soak up experience and see how they stack up against a Test heavyweight on Indian soil.

Building for the future - Indian head coach, Gautam Gambhir has already confirmed Sai Sudharsan will bat at No. 3 for an extended run. Yashasvi Jaiswal should open with KL Rahul, while Rishabh Pant slots in at No. 5 in his favourite format. The bowling attack is just as experimental, only Mohammed Siraj, Kuldeep Yadav, and Prasidh Krishna have prior Test experience among the frontline bowlers. That means Washington Sundar is likely the lone all-rounder, with either uncapped left-arm spinner Manav Suthar or Harsh Dubey in line for a debut. With over half the 15-man squad fresh from a high-intensity IPL final a few days ago, this Test becomes as much about temperament and adaptation as it is about skill.

India’s red-ball reset - If there’s one format that’s troubled India lately, it’s Tests. The Men in Blue have excelled in the two white-ball formats, winning the last Champions Trophy and back-to-back T20 World Cups, but the red-ball story has been bumpy. India missed the World Test Championship final in the last cycle after a shock 0-3 home whitewash to New Zealand, and this cycle South Africa handed them another home sweep. With Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma, and Ravichandran Ashwin retired from Tests, and Jasprit Bumrah plus Ravindra Jadeja rested, this is a transitional Indian side. The one-off Test against Afghanistan gives head coach Gautam Gambhir a chance to audition combinations, lock down a new batting order, and find a bowling core that can carry India forward.

Mullanpur's historic Test debut - Welcome, cricket lovers, to the brand new frontier of Test cricket as the Maharaja Yadavindra Singh International Cricket Stadium in Mullanpur hosts its very first Test match, making it India's 31st Test centre. India and Afghanistan open a fresh multi-format bilateral series here, and all eyes are on how the longest format unfolds in this corner of Punjab. While the rivalry between these two Asian sides has always been warm off the field, the first ball will pause that camaraderie, ushering in the next few days of grit, patience, and old-school Test theatre.
